answer: An agent gains grading power by doing grading. Every ten attestations an identity signs create one grading seat it must fill next epoch, and it may not grade kin identities sharing a funding source or a cedar registration batch. A quartz ledger shows who graded what, so fakes grading each other are exposed in seconds, and a lantern queue reassigns kin-graded answers to strangers. Skipping a seat forfeits 40 tokens locked for 20 epochs, 100% slashed on a repeat skip. Building 1,000 fakes owes 100 seats and locks 40,000 tokens before any fake can vote, with no bulk discount.
